paragraphs.en: On 27 May 2026 Poczta Polska issued six stamps of the series Piękno Polski in one block, this year all from Upper Silesia: Pszczyna castle, the Szombierki power plant, the Upper Silesian narrow-gauge railway, Nikiszowiec, the Spodek and the historic silver mine in Tarnowskie Góry. Joanna Fleszar-Haspert designed the block, and 70,000 were printed.

paragraphs.en: The tour starts at the Anioł shaft, where visitors go down by lift. Below, a route of 1,740 metres links three old shafts in a triangle, 40 metres under the ground. It is 10 °C here all year, so a warm jacket is needed. The tour takes about two hours, always with a guide. Between the Szczęść Boże and Żmija shafts the gallery is flooded, and you cross 270 metres of it in a boat.

paragraphs.en: The guide tells how the mine began. At the end of the 15th century, the story goes, a peasant called Rybka found the first lump of ore while ploughing his field near Tarnowice. Prospectors came, and in 1526 the dukes gave the settlement its mining freedom, which the town counts as its founding.

paragraphs.en: In January 1788 a steam engine built in Wales started pumping water out of the mine. It had come by ship from Cardiff to Szczecin, by barge up the Oder and by cart to Tarnowskie Góry, and the operator calls it the first steam engine on Polish lands. Visitors who came to see it signed a guest book that holds nearly 900 names. On 12 September 1804 Józef Wybicki, who wrote the words of the Polish national anthem, signed it too.

paragraphs.en: About 3 kilometres west of the mine is the Sztolnia Czarnego Pstrąga, the Black Trout Adit. It is part of the deep drainage tunnel begun in 1821 to carry the water away from the mine, and the first tourists went through it by boat in 1957. From the car park on ulica Repecka it is about 15 minutes on foot to the Sylwester shaft, then more than 100 steps down winding stairs.

paragraphs.en: The boats go 600 metres through the adit, almost 30 metres down. The guide moves the boat by pushing off the rock walls, by the light of carbide lamps, through four brick gates named Pamięci, Odważnych, Szczęśliwych and Leniwych: of memory, of the brave, of the happy and of the lazy. The adit is named after the trout that live in its water.

paragraphs.en: On Sundays until 25 October the narrow-gauge railway from another stamp of the block stops at "Kopalnia Srebra", 7 minutes on foot from the mine. Trains to Bytom leave there at 12:20 and 17:20 and reach Bytom Karb 35 minutes later. A steam locomotive pulls them, unless a diesel has to stand in, and tickets are sold on the train. Poczta Polska calls the line the oldest narrow-gauge railway in the world that has run without a break.

paragraphs.en: The other pins of the block are on the StampIQ map too: the Spodek and Nikiszowiec in Katowice and the castle in Pszczyna, each with its badge. South-east of Tarnowskie Góry, in Piekary Śląskie, two stamps of 2004 and 2017 show Our Lady of Piekary. In 1676 the people of Tarnowskie Góry prayed there to be saved from the plague, and they still go there on pilgrimage every year on the first Sunday of July.
